lines.text: Long jobs are the worst. You either wait in the dark, or drown in step two done messages.
Now Agent R Q agents can post one card that updates while you watch. It's built on Eh two U I, the open standard for agent interfaces.
Ada asks the agent to build and check the website, with a live card.
It posts one card. Four steps, all queued, and an empty chart.
Then it edits that same card. Install and build are done, in five seconds each.
The tests are running now, and the chart fills in as each step ends.
Fifteen seconds in all. Four steps done, in the same place in the thread.
An update is an edit, not a new message. So it sends no notification. The card is just there, current, when you look.
The checks come back as a card too. The build and tests pass. Three hundred and four lint warnings get a yellow mark.
One card that moves, instead of a stream of pings. What long job would you watch live? Tell us in the comments, and try it at Agent R Q dot com.
